known_research_boundaries: The episode is a practical shopping puzzle at Fort Albany,1733. Start with twenty hooks versus a blanket, then reveal why 'one beaver' is a unit rather than a simple animal count. Anchor numeric statements to the original Dobbs1744scan; pp.193–194 were visually inspected on2026-10-09. Original lists blanket6,breeches3,8knives/1,20hooks/1,kettle1lb/1,sugar2lb/1,broadcloth1yard/2,thread1lb/2. Modern heritage-derived tables often flatten the right column and misstate blanket/breeches prices; the UVic compilation independently mistranscribes other rows. Reject both for numeric authority. Use two source-based surprises: a kettle's weight changes its price, and Indigenous customers actively assessed imported cloth. Context is specific and relationships unequal; neither naive-barter caricature nor universal golden-age claim. No actual1733shopping receipt, exact household budget, exact fort plan or finished costume reference is claimed. The final six-unit choice is our arithmetic demonstration. Primary text is colonial and argumentative, not neutral access to Indigenous voices; source labels remain clear. Source-image and garment shape gate is separate from these factual checks.
